title: Repository Guidelines
text: gwasplot R package organized standard package conventions. - R/: package source code (manhattan.R, locuszoom.R, annotate.R, etc.). - src/: C++ helpers via Rcpp (RcppExports.cpp, qqplot.cpp). - man/: generated Rd documentation (hand-edit). - data/: packaged .rda reference datasets. - data-raw/: scripts used build data artifacts. - .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml: CI workflow site/docs publishing. - renv/ renv.lock: reproducible dependency environment.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Run repository root: - R -q -e "renv::restore()": install locked dependencies. - R -q -e "devtools::load_all()": load package interactive development. - R -q -e "devtools::document()": regenerate NAMESPACE man/*.Rd roxygen comments. - R -q -e "devtools::test()": run testthat suite. - R -q -e "devtools::check()" R CMD check .: run package checks. - R -q -e "pkgdown::build_site_github_pages(new_process = FALSE, install = FALSE)": build docs site (matches CI). - air format R/: format R sources (config air.toml). See CLAUDE.md high-level architecture (DuckDB-backed GWASFormatter object, S3 method pattern, -place filtering pipeline).

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Format R sources air (air.toml: 80-col, 2-space indent). Keep formatting-changes commit, separate behavior changes. Prefer snake_case function object names (example, reformat_summary_statistics). Keep exported APIs documented roxygen2 (#') regenerate docs devtools::document(). Follow existing S3 method patterns (GWASFormatter, data.frame, tbl_df) adding generic behavior.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Tests live tests/testthat/ (testthat 3e), named test-<feature>.R. opening PR: - Run devtools::test() devtools::check(); resolve warnings/errors. - Add testthat tests tests/testthat/ non-trivial logic. - Manually validate changed plotting/annotation paths small GWAS sample.

title: Repository Guidelines
text: Keep commit messages short, imperative, specific (examples history: fix manhattan bug, improve API qqplot function). Separate refactors behavior changes possible. concise summary user-visible changes, linked issue(s) relevant, representative plots/screenshots visualization changes, confirmation devtools::document() devtools::check() run.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: reformat_summary_statistics(file_path) (R/reformat.R) main entry point. returns GWASFormatter R6 object wraps: - $con — DuckDB connection (db_connect() opens local.duckdb) - $data — lazy dbplyr tbl current active table - $table_name / $source_table_name — active original table names construction detects input format (detect_format()), standardizes column names (reformat_names() via reformat_lookup()), undoes LOG10P, maps chr23→chrX, builds ID (CHROM_POS_REF_ALT), materializes uniquely-named DuckDB table. unique naming deliberate: multiple GWASFormatter objects can coexist one working directory without clobbering shared summary_stats table. title: Basic GWAS Plots
text: helper generates data frame standard columns CHROM, POS, PVALUE, distributing variants proportionally across chromosomes optionally injecting genome-wide significant signals.
code: library(gwasplot) #> ℹ Setting duckdb_max_memory to 6GB, using 80% of available system memory. #> ℹ Change this with options(duckdb_max_memory = 'XGB') #>  #> Attaching package: 'gwasplot' #> The following object is masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     qqplot  # Approximate chromosome sizes (Mb, hg38) chr_mb <- c(249, 242, 198, 190, 181, 171, 159, 145, 138, 134,             135, 133, 115, 107, 102,  90,  83,  80,  59,  63, 47, 51)  sim_gwas <- function(n_total, hits = NULL,                      chroms = paste0("chr", 1:22)) {   sizes <- chr_mb[seq_along(chroms)]   dfs <- Map(function(ch, mb) {     n <- max(1L, round(n_total * mb / sum(sizes)))     data.frame(       CHROM  = ch,       POS    = sort(sample.int(mb * 1e6L, n)),       PVALUE = runif(n)     )   }, chroms, sizes)   df <- do.call(rbind, dfs)   for (h in hits) {     idx <- df$CHROM == h$chrom & abs(df$POS - h$pos) < h$window     df$PVALUE[idx] <- runif(sum(idx), h$pmin, h$pmax)   }   df }  set.seed(42) gwas_df <- sim_gwas(   n_total = 500000,   hits = list(     list(chrom = "chr2",  pos = 135e6, window = 5e5, pmin = 1e-15, pmax = 1e-8),     list(chrom = "chr5",  pos =  50e6, window = 5e5, pmin = 1e-12, pmax = 1e-8),     list(chrom = "chr11", pos =  70e6, window = 5e5, pmin = 1e-20, pmax = 1e-8),     list(chrom = "chr17", pos =  30e6, window = 5e5, pmin = 1e-10, pmax = 1e-8)   ) )  head(gwas_df) #>        CHROM   POS    PVALUE #> chr1.1  chr1   611 0.4831109 #> chr1.2  chr1  1527 0.6988779 #> chr1.3  chr1  9474 0.8769163 #> chr1.4  chr1 28440 0.3938541 #> chr1.5  chr1 54879 0.7036494 #> chr1.6  chr1 58418 0.5482878

title: Identifying Independent Loci
text: simulation places three tight clusters significant variants chromosomes 1, 3, 4.
code: library(gwasplot) #> ℹ Setting duckdb_max_memory to 6GB, using 80% of available system memory. #> ℹ Change this with options(duckdb_max_memory = 'XGB') #>  #> Attaching package: 'gwasplot' #> The following object is masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     qqplot  # Approximate chromosome sizes (Mb, hg38) chr_mb <- c(249, 242, 198, 190, 181, 171, 159, 145, 138, 134,             135, 133, 115, 107, 102,  90,  83,  80,  59,  63, 47, 51)  sim_gwas <- function(n_total, hits = NULL,                      chroms = paste0("chr", 1:22)) {   sizes <- chr_mb[seq_along(chroms)]   dfs <- Map(function(ch, mb) {     n <- max(1L, round(n_total * mb / sum(sizes)))     data.frame(       CHROM  = ch,       POS    = sort(sample.int(mb * 1e6L, n)),       PVALUE = runif(n)     )   }, chroms, sizes)   df <- do.call(rbind, dfs)   for (h in hits) {     idx <- df$CHROM == h$chrom & abs(df$POS - h$pos) < h$window     df$PVALUE[idx] <- runif(sum(idx), h$pmin, h$pmax)   }   df }  set.seed(123) gwas_df <- sim_gwas(   n_total = 100000,   chroms  = paste0("chr", 1:5),   hits    = list(     list(chrom = "chr1", pos = 100e6, window = 2e6, pmin = 1e-20, pmax = 1e-8),     list(chrom = "chr3", pos =  60e6, window = 2e6, pmin = 1e-15, pmax = 1e-8),     list(chrom = "chr4", pos =  80e6, window = 2e6, pmin = 1e-12, pmax = 1e-8)   ) )  nrow(gwas_df) #> [1] 100000
